channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Egypt on edge steps up its defenses as Israel–Iran conflict shakes the region
item.description: Egypt has elevated its state of alert following the heightened tension in the Middle East, particularly due to Israeli strikes on Iran and Iran's subsequent retaliation across the region.

item.title: 10 most beautiful universities in Africa, according to latest ranking
item.description: University life in Africa is defined as much by campus beauty as academics, with stunning landscapes, green lawns, mountains, lagoons, and palm-lined paths — led by the University of Cape Town.

item.title: Global shipping carriers, international airlines pivot back to Africa route as Middle East crisis intensifies
item.description: Fresh turmoil in the Middle East is once again redrawing global trade and aviation maps, pushing shipping lines and airlines back toward longer and costlier Africa-bound routes.

item.title: Niger becomes second AES state to sign Trump’s $128M health deal
item.description: Niger has formally signed a $128 million health deal with the United States, making it the second of the three Alliance of Sahel States (AES) to join Washington’s “America First” Global Health Strategy.

item.title: After years of disruption, South Africa lands $473m investment from world’s second-largest miner
item.description: The world’s second-largest mining company, Rio Tinto, has approved a $473 million expansion of its South African mineral sands operation, marking a decisive step toward restoring stability after years of violent disruption and governance setbacks.

item.title: AMNI mobilises rig to Okoro as Tunde Afolabi targets 12,000 bpd offshore boost
item.description: AMNI International Petroleum Development Company has moved a drilling rig to the Okoro offshore field in Nigeria, beginning a three-well campaign aimed at raising output to more than 12,000 barrels of oil a day. The company described the rig’s arrival as a major step in its wider plan to boost production from existing assets and strengthen its position among leading indigenous operators.

item.title: Sawiris: inflation forces smaller homes in Egypt's property market
item.description: Egyptian billionaire Naguib Sawiris, chair and chief executive of Ora Developer, has warned that Egypt’s property developers are being pushed into building smaller homes as inflation and rising construction costs undermine what ordinary buyers can afford.

item.title: U.S. sanctions Rwanda’s military as m23 conflict escalates in Eastern Congo
item.description: The United States on Monday announced sanctions against the Rwanda Defence Force and several senior commanders, accusing them of helping fuel the worsening conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Washington said Rwandan troops must immediately pull back from the mineral-rich region, where fighting has escalated despite a recent peace agreement.

item.title: FULL LIST: African countries that signed Trump’s controversial health deals
item.description: A sweeping shift in the United States global health policy under former President Donald Trump has stirred debate across Africa, as Washington replaces large multilateral aid programmes with bilateral health agreements tied to stricter conditions.

item.title: Egypt net foreign assets hit record $29.5 billion in January 2026
item.description: Egypt’s central bank and commercial banks now hold more foreign currency than ever before. On Monday, the central bank said net foreign assets, a key measure that shows total foreign money held minus foreign debts, rose by $4.02 billion in January. The new total reached a record $29.54 billion.
